deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two unrelated pieces of work. The formulas are written upside down relative to the German prose, so the sheet was turned and reused.

(A) GERMAN PROSE: a draft of the topology of surfaces.
Riemann drafts the opening of his theory of connectivity: 'Die Untersuchung der [zusammenhängenden] Fläche erfolgt durch ihre Zerlegung durch Querschnitte, d.h. Linien, welche von einem Begrenzungspunkte durch das Innere nach einem Begrenzungspunkte gehen ...'. A further clause says that the endpoints of later cuts may lie in the part of the boundary newly created by earlier cuts ('... in dem zur Begrenzung neu hinzugekommenen Theile, also [auf] Punkte der Querschnitte liegen').
It then gives the definition: 'Eine zusammenhängende Fläche heißt, wenn sie durch jeden Querschnitt in getrennte Stücke zerfällt, eine einfach zusammenhängende.'
Next comes the heading 'Lehrsatz I.', with no statement written out. By analogy with the 1857 paper it is presumably the invariance of the connectivity number under systems of cross-cuts.
This is essentially the wording of Riemann's dissertation (1851, art. 6) and of 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857), 'Lehrsätze aus der analysis situs'.

(B) FORMULAS: a heat-conduction problem continued from the previous page.

B.1 The problem.
- Unknown: u(x,t) for x>0, t>0, with u_t = α² u_xx.
- Initial condition: u(x,0) = 0.
- Boundary condition at x = 0 (Newtonian cooling / Robin condition): ∂u/∂x − ν u + ω = 0. The previous page writes 'a' where this page writes ω.

B.2 The elementary solution.
- Riemann takes u_1(x,t) = ∫_∞^{x/(2α√(t−t_1))} e^{−q²} dq.
- In modern terms u_1 = −(√π/2) erfc(x/(2α√(t−t_1))), which solves the heat equation.
- Its x-derivative is ∂u_1/∂x = e^{−x²/(4α²(t−t_1))} / (2α√(t−t_1)). This is written on the page.
- At x = 0, u_1 = Δ, where Δ := ∫_∞^0 e^{−q²} dq = −√π/2.

B.3 Duhamel superposition.
- He sets u = ∫_0^t u_1(x, t−τ) ρ(τ) dτ, with density ρ = φ' (the note 'ϱ_t = φ'').
- The boundary condition at x = 0 then becomes a Volterra/Abel integral equation, the content of 'Lehrsatz I' on the formula side:
  ∫_0^t [ 1/(2α√(t−τ)) − νΔ ] ρ(τ) dτ = ω, up to sign conventions.
- The page also carries the variant ∫_0^t (e^{−x²/(4α²(t−τ))}/(2α√(t−τ)) − νΔ) ρ dτ = ω, i.e. the kernel before setting x = 0.
- On the previous page this equation is solved by a series in powers of t^{1/2} with Gamma-function (Π) coefficients. The series sums to e^{α²ν²t} times erfc-type terms.

B.4 Change of variable in the representation of u.
- From the previous page: u = ∫_{x/(2α√t)}^∞ e^{−y²} φ(t − x²/(4α²y²)) dy.
- Here he puts z = 1/y² (the inference is mine). Then τ = t − x² z/(4α²) = t − s, where s = x² z/(4α²).
- Result (normalization constants mine): u = ½ ∫_0^{4α²t/x²} e^{−1/z} z^{−3/2} φ(t − x² z/(4α²)) dz.
- The side note 'z = xx/(4ααt)' records the reciprocal of the upper limit.

B.5 Differentiation in x.
- ∂u/∂x has two parts:
  - a boundary term from the moving upper limit, −[integrand at z = 4α²t/x²]·φ(0)·(8α²t/x³). The factor d/dx(4α²t/x²) = −8α²t/x³ appears explicitly.
  - an integral term −∫_0^{4α²t/x²} (…) φ'(t − x²z/(4α²)) · (2xz/(4α²)) dz.
- He also writes u − Δ(…) as an integral of the same kind, and records the elementary case t = t_1, u = 0, with (u − Δ)/x expressed through 1/(2α√(t−t_1)).

B.6 Integration by parts and an interchange of order.
- Lower right of the page: he needs integrals like ∫_∞^{1/√s} e^{−q²} dq integrated once more in s (the iterated error function), and ∫ e^{−q²} q^{−2} dq.
- Integration by parts gives ∫ e^{−q²}/q² dq = −e^{−q²}/q − 2∫ e^{−q²} dq.
- Hence ∫_{1/√s}^∞ e^{−q²} q^{−2} dq = √s e^{−1/s} − 2 ∫_{1/√s}^∞ e^{−q²} dq. The page has '−√s e^{−1/s} + 2∫_∞^{1/√s} e^{−qq} ∂q', i.e. the same expression for the reversed orientation ∫_∞^{1/√s}.
- The last line, 's > z > 1/qq', gives the region for exchanging the order of the double integral ∫∫ e^{−q²} dq dz (Fubini). This computes ∫_0^s u_1 dz in closed form.

B.7 Remaining fragments.
- 'φ_1 = −½ p x^{−3/2} + …' and 'px + q + rx' at the top are trial or auxiliary expressions.
- '…/(2x³)' at the top left matches the factor 8α²t/x³ from the boundary term.

Purpose of B overall: obtain the closed-form solution of the half-line heat problem with radiation (Robin) boundary condition. In modern form: u = (ω/ν)[erfc(x/(2α√t)) − e^{νx+ν²α²t} erfc(x/(2α√t) + να√t)].
errors: Sign/orientation of the integration-by-parts formula '−√s e^{−1/s} + 2∫_∞^{1/√s} e^{−qq}dq' cannot be fully confirmed from the image. It equals the integral ∫_{1/√s}^∞ e^{−q²}/q² dq up to orientation of the limits. A ± slip is possible but not certain.

The 'Lehrsatz I' formula line is garbled (leading factor ν/2, right side '2αω + νΔφt'). As read it is not dimensionally consistent with the cleaner second form ∫_0^t (e^{−x²/(4α²(t−τ))}/(2α√(t−τ)) − νΔ) ρ dτ = ω. It appears to be a first attempt, then rewritten.

The argument of φ in the z-integrals must be t − x² z/(4α²), not t − x²/(4α² z). Only the former is consistent with the upper limit 4α²t/x² and with the boundary-term factor −8α²t/x³. This is probably a transcription issue, not Riemann's error.
Constant factors (½, z^{−3/2}, e^{−1/z}) in the z-representation are not legible and are reconstructed; the manuscript lines are incomplete scratch work.

results.what: Definition of cross-cuts (Querschnitte) and of a simply connected surface: a connected surface that is split into separate pieces by every cross-cut. Includes the clause that cuts may end on earlier cuts. Followed by 'Lehrsatz I'.
results.modern_name: Simple connectivity / connectivity number via cross-cuts (Riemann's Querschnitte, precursor of the genus and first Betti number)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (dissertation 1851; Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857)

results.what: Elementary solution u_1 = ∫_∞^{x/(2α√(t−t_1))} e^{−q²}dq of the heat equation and its x-derivative e^{−x²/(4α²(t−t_1))}/(2α√(t−t_1))
results.modern_name: Error-function (erfc) similarity solution of the heat equation

results.what: Duhamel superposition reducing the Robin (radiation) boundary condition ∂u/∂x − νu + ω = 0 to a Volterra/Abel integral equation ∫_0^t[1/(2α√(t−τ)) − νΔ]ρ(τ)dτ = ω
results.modern_name: Duhamel's principle plus Abel integral equation (second-kind Volterra equation with weakly singular kernel); half-line heat problem with Newton cooling
results.usually_credited_to: Duhamel (1833), Abel (1823); closed erfc solution standard in Carslaw–Jaeger

results.what: Change of variables z = 1/y² in u = ∫ e^{−y²} φ(t − x²/(4α²y²)) dy and differentiation under the integral, including the boundary term from the x-dependent limit
Integration by parts ∫_{1/√s}^∞ e^{−q²}q^{−2}dq = √s e^{−1/s} − 2∫_{1/√s}^∞ e^{−q²}dq, and interchange of order of a double integral to compute the iterated erfc

deep.surprise_reason: The topology text is a draft of Riemann's well-known definitions of cross-cuts and simple connectivity (1851/1857). The heat-conduction calculation is a routine Duhamel/Abel-integral-equation treatment of the radiation boundary condition, consistent with his known lectures on partial differential equations. Nothing here anticipates later work.

u_1 = ∫_∞^{x/(2α√t)} e^{−q²}dq solves u_t = α² u_xx (should be 0)
With φ ≡ 1 the z-representation ½∫_0^{4α²t/x²} e^{−1/z} z^{−3/2} dz equals ∫_{x/(2α√t)}^∞ e^{−y²}dy (should be 0)

transcription_corrections: The formula block is written upside down relative to the German text (sheet rotated). The transcription mixes the two orientations.

Prose should read approximately: 'Die Untersuchung der [zusammenhängenden] Fläche erfolgt durch ihre Zerlegung durch Querschnitte, d.h. Linien, welche von einem Begrenzungspunkte durch das Innere nach einem Begrenzungspunkte gehen; ... in dem zur Begrenzung neu hinzugekommenen Theile, also [auf] Punkte[n] der Querschnitte liegen.'
Definition sentence: 'Eine zusammenhängende Fläche heißt, wenn sie durch jeden Querschnitt in getrennte Stücke zerfällt, eine einfach zusammenhängende' (cf. Riemann 1857).
In the z-integrals the argument is φ(t − (xx/4αα) z), not φ(t − xx/(4αα z)), consistent with the upper limit t·4αα/xx.
'1664/2x³' at the top left is likely a factor such as '16αα.../2x³' related to 8ααt/x³, not the number 1664.
'∂u/∂x = e^{−xx/(4αα(t−t_1))} 1/(2α√(t−t_1))' refers to the elementary solution u_1, not to the general u.
